claims.claim_text: Global liquidity is contracting, driven by dollar strength and eroding collateral values, creating a fragile and deteriorating financial environment.
reasoning_chain: Step 1: A stronger US dollar tightens global dollar liquidity by raising the cost of dollar-denominated borrowing and reducing the value of foreign collateral in dollar terms.
Step 2: Weakening collateral values reduce the capacity of the financial system to generate credit and leverage, compressing the effective money supply.
Step 3: The system is operating at a record-high collateral multiplier, meaning any decline in collateral quality or value has an amplified negative effect on total liquidity.
Step 4: The combination of these forces produces a net decline in nominal global liquidity, tightening financial conditions across the board.
